newsitem.title: FRANCE: Lazard source denies report of succession crisis.
newsitem.headline: Lazard source denies report of succession crisis.

text.p: A partner of Lazard Freres on Thursday denied a report in the French afternoon daily Le Monde that a "succession crisis" was brewing at the blue-chip investment banking group.
"There is no foundation to this article," said the partner, who preferred to remain anonymous.
The current chairman of Lazard Freres and Co and its two affiliated partnerships, New York-based Lazard Freres and London-based Lazard Brothers and Co, is Michel David-Weill, 64.

Le Monde said a power struggle was under way at the prestigious merchant bank and that David-Weill had fallen out with his son-in-law Edouard Stern, 42, recruited in 1992, who, the newspaper said, had been his heir apparent.
It added the investment house was having trouble finding replacements for its some of its most senior figures who were approaching retirement.
The traditionally discreet 150-year-old advisory firm has been involved in some high-profile mergers and acquisitions in recent years.

The three Lazard houses were formally linked together in 1984 through the creation of Lazard Partners. Since then, the association among the three houses has resulted in ever-closer working relationships.
They are engaged mainly in corporate advisory services, including mergers and acquisitions, trading activites, capital market services and asset management for individuals and institutions.
